title: Theming
description: Built-in light and dark themes, design tokens as CSS variables, and how to create your own theme.

builtIn.title: Built-in themes
builtIn.text: The React library ships three themes: light, dark and github-dark. Pick one with the theme prop of ConfigProvider, or keep the default "auto", which follows the operating system's color scheme and updates live when it changes.

live.title: Try it
live.text: This switcher drives the theme of the whole documentation site. The components below, and every page, update instantly because they only read CSS variables.
live.alert: Components re-theme without re-rendering: only the CSS variables on <html> change.

values.title: Accepted theme values
values.text: The theme prop of ConfigProvider (and useAutoTheme / applyThemeStyles) accepts:
values.auto: Default. Uses light or dark according to prefers-color-scheme and follows changes.
values.githubDark: A dark theme based on GitHub's dark palette.
values.object: A complete theme object (every base token, plus optional semantic and component tokens). Usually built by spreading a built-in theme.
values.pair: Two theme objects; the one matching the system color scheme is applied and switches automatically.

how.title: How it works
how.p1: A theme is a flat map of token names to CSS values. ConfigProvider writes every entry as a CSS custom property named --<token> in the inline style of the <html> element:
how.p2: Component styles only reference these variables (for example background: var(--primary-color)), so changing theme never re-renders React components. The stylesheet also declares every token on :root, so components are styled with the light values even before (or without) a ConfigProvider.

custom.title: Custom themes
custom.text: Create a theme by spreading a built-in one and overriding the tokens you need, then pass it to ConfigProvider. Pass a { light, dark } pair to keep following the system color scheme. Semantic tokens such as hover, subtle background and focus ring colors are derived from the base tokens, so overriding primary-color is usually enough.

colorProps.title: Color and variant props
colorProps.color: Every component picks its semantic color with the same color prop, typed from the shared ColorScheme: primary, neutral, success, warning, danger or info (some components accept a documented subset). It is always a theme role, never a raw CSS color: to recolor a component, change the theme tokens or the component's CSS custom properties.
colorProps.variant: variant only selects the visual style, with the same meaning everywhere: solid (filled with the color, inverse text), subtle (tinted background), outline (transparent background, colored border and text) and ghost (transparent, no border). Components add their own styles where needed (Tabs line / enclosed, Input filled ...).

css.title: Overriding tokens with CSS
css.text: You can also set tokens from a plain stylesheet. Keep in mind where each value is defined:
css.note: ConfigProvider writes the active theme as inline styles on <html>, which take precedence over :root rules in a stylesheet. Tokens set by the theme need !important to be overridden globally; component tokens (btn-*, card-*, avatar-*) are not set by the built-in themes and can be defined normally.

tokens.title: Token reference
tokens.text: Every token is available as var(--<token>). Swatches show the value of the current theme.
tokens.semanticText: Optional (SemanticThemeProps). Their defaults are derived from the base tokens with color-mix(); the built-in dark themes set some of them explicitly.
tokens.rolesText: Each role color gets derived hover, active, subtle (tinted background), border and text tokens, e.g. --primary-color-hover or --danger-color-subtle.
tokens.componentText: Optional per-component overrides (ComponentThemeProps). Components fall back to the semantic tokens when they are not set.

snippets.source:
<!-- what ConfigProvider writes on the document root -->
<html style="--primary-color: #58a6ff; --background-color: #0d1117; ...">
